title: Envisioning Emerging Technologies
author: Envisioning
frame: Radial chart in six sectors (Neurotechnology and cognitive technologies; Health; Agricultural; Nanotechnology and materials science; Energy; Digital and communication), numbered 1-88 clockwise from 12 o'clock. Distance from the centre is time: concentric year lines run from about 2014 (inner edge of the grid) to about 2027 (outer edge), with labelled thick lines at 2015, 2020 and 2025 and a thin line for every year. Each technology is a rounded bar (not strictly radial): its inner end is 'scientifically viable', the white numbered dot on it is the 'mainstream point', and its outer end is 'financially viable'. Legend ("TIMELINE"), verbatim: FINANCIALLY VIABLE: "The point when products and services using the technology are generally available on Kickstarter." MAINSTREAM POINT: "Predicted point when the technology becomes avilable for prototyping in R&D labs, or when VCs and startups start investing in it." SCIENTIFICALLY VIABLE: "Concept-stage, unstable, unlikely, sci-fi inspired, billion-dollar budgets. Only Google, governments and universities really invest at this risk level." Method: on the 4960x3507 image the ring centre is (2476.5, 1751.5) px (fixed from symmetric ring lines on both axes); year lines were measured at r=695.5 px (2015), 860.5 (2020), 1023 (2025), one line every 32.75 px, so year = 2015 + (r - 695.5)/32.75. Bars and numbered dots were segmented by colour; the mainstream year is the radius of the dot centre, the milestone years are the radii of the bar end-cap centres; all are rounded to the nearest year. A dot within 0.12 year of a half-year is medium confidence.
quote: Mainstream point: "Predicted point when the technology becomes avilable for prototyping in R&D labs, or when VCs and startups start investing in it." Methodology: "Timelines should be interpreted relatively, not literally."

entries.label: Predictive crime prevention
entries.claim: Predictive crime prevention reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2026
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.0, on the 2026 line (read as 2026). Bar from 2021.8 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2022, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Neural network computing.
entries.interpretation: The use of sociometric sensors coupled with neural networked computers to statistically determine the probability of crime (or other anti-social behavior) taking place before it happens.

entries.label: Predictive group sentiment analysis
entries.claim: Predictive group sentiment analysis reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2023
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2023.5, midway between the 2023 and 2024 lines (read as 2023). Bar from 2022.6 to 2026.8: scientifically viable ~2023, financially viable ~2027. Sub-area: Neural network computing.
entries.interpretation: Predicting the likely behavior of large groups of people based on sociometric input variables like social tension, weather variation, pedestrian flows and degree of agitation is becoming increasingly possible.

entries.label: Neural network image recognition
entries.claim: Neural network image recognition reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2021
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2021.0, on the 2021 line (read as 2021). Bar from 2013.8 to 2021.7: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2022. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Neural network computing.
entries.interpretation: Using hundreds of thousands of processor cores programmed to algorithmically determine the content of a given image. Different from reverse image search, neural network image recognition has the capacity to successfully understand the photo of, for example, a cat, based on thousands of cat pictures.

entries.label: Emotion tracking
entries.claim: Emotion tracking reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2018.4, midway between the 2018 and 2019 lines (read as 2018). Bar from 2014.4 to 2018.7: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2019. Sub-area: Neural network computing.
entries.interpretation: Using sensors, computer vision and algorithms to correctly identify the likely emotions displayed by individuals in a crowd. Useful in airports and other high-risk facilities.

entries.label: Proactive software agents
entries.claim: Proactive software agents reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2016
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2016.5, midway between the 2016 and 2017 lines (read as 2016). Bar from 2013.8 to 2016.7: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2017. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Neural network computing. The poster's description for this item ends with a pasted fragment of item 1's text ('...potential usages.etworked computers to statistically determine the probability of crime...'); the interpretation keeps only the first part.
entries.interpretation: Software applications with the capacity of discerning and predicting likely future needs for whomever is being served. Intelligently scheduling meetings, sorting email and selectively notifying the user are potential usages.

entries.label: Neuroprosthetics
entries.claim: Neuroprosthetics reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2026
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.2, between the 2026 and 2027 lines, nearer 2026 (read as 2026). Bar from 2022.1 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2022, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Extended cognition.
entries.interpretation: Neural devices capable of substituting motor, sensory or cognitive modalities that might have been damaged as a result of an injury or a disease. Applications include neural enhancements, advanced cognitive features and extended physiological senses.

entries.label: Next-generation neuropharmacology
entries.claim: Next-generation neuropharmacology reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2022
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2021.5, midway between the 2021 and 2022 lines (read as 2022). Bar from 2018.8 to 2023.0: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2023. Sub-area: Extended cognition.
entries.interpretation: Both behavioral and molecular neuropharmacology are benefitting from rapidly accelerating change. With an increase in technology and improved understanding of the nervous system, the development of drugs will continue to rise with an increase in drug sensitivity and specificity.

entries.label: Micromachined ultrasonic transducers
entries.claim: Micromachined ultrasonic transducers reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2020
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2019.5, midway between the 2019 and 2020 lines (read as 2020). Bar from 2016.2 to 2019.8: scientifically viable ~2016, financially viable ~2020. Sub-area: Extended cognition.
entries.interpretation: A relatively new concept in the field of ultrasonic capacitative transducers where the energy transduction is due to change in capacitance. Can be used to remotely improve alertness, awareness in soldiers, etc.

entries.label: Neural biofeedback
entries.claim: Neural biofeedback reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2016
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2015.6, midway between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016). Bar from 2013.8 to 2017.4: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2017. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Extended cognition.
entries.interpretation: Biofeedback using real-time EEG or fMRI to illustrate brain activity, often with a goal of controlling the central nervous actions.

entries.label: Brain-to-brain interfaces
entries.claim: Brain-to-brain interfaces reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2027
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.9, on the 2027 line (read as 2027). Bar from 2025.1 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2025, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: The hypothetical implementation of brain interfaces that translate thoughts, sensations or impulses into digital signal, converting the data back into the recipient's brain to enable a certain response from both ends.

entries.label: Optogenetic implants in humans
entries.claim: Optogenetic implants in humans reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2026
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.5, midway between the 2026 and 2027 lines (read as 2026). Bar from 2022.0 to 2026.5: scientifically viable ~2022, financially viable ~2026. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: The combination of genetic and optical methods to control specific events in targeted cells of living tissue, even within freely moving mammals and other animals, with the temporal precision (millisecond timescale) needed to keep pace with functioning intact biological systems.

entries.label: Next-gen BCI
entries.claim: Next-gen BCI reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2022
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.5, midway between the 2022 and 2023 lines (read as 2022). Bar from 2020.9 to 2027.2: scientifically viable ~2021, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: Hypothetical interfaces to be used for assisting, augmenting, or repairing human cognitive or sensory-motor functions and communicate thoughts and intentions to the Internet.

entries.label: Transcranial magnetic stimulation
entries.claim: Transcranial magnetic stimulation reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2019
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2019.3, between the 2019 and 2020 lines, nearer 2019 (read as 2019). Bar from 2013.8 to 2022.4: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2022. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: TMS is a noninvasive method to cause depolarization or hyperpolarization in the neurons of the brain using electromagnetic induction to induce weak electric currents using a rapidly changing magnetic field. This can cause activity in specific or general parts of the brain with minimal discomfort, allowing the functioning and interconnections of the brain to be studied.

entries.label: High-resolution fMRI
entries.claim: High-resolution fMRI reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2018.3, between the 2018 and 2019 lines, nearer 2018 (read as 2018). Bar from 2014.5 to 2019.4: scientifically viable ~2015, financially viable ~2019. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: The next generation of functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging involves increasing the spatial and temporal resolution of the imagery. We are likely to see a 14-tesla machines becoming common (as opposed to today's 3-tesla).

entries.label: EEG Brain-to-computer interfaces
entries.claim: EEG Brain-to-computer interfaces reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2014
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2014.3, between the 2014 and 2015 lines, nearer 2014 (read as 2014). Bar from 2013.8 to 2020.3: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2020. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Neural interfaces.
entries.interpretation: Electroencephalography remains the most feasible practice of executing and implementing brain to brain interfaces. It represents the best temporal-resolution tool for getting a picture of the brain in action, is portable, non-invasive and extremely affordable compared to other methods.

entries.label: Enhanced organs
entries.claim: Enhanced organs reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2027
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.7, between the 2026 and 2027 lines, nearer 2027 (read as 2027). Bar from 2024.2 to 2027.1: scientifically viable ~2024, financially viable ~2027. Sub-area: Augmentation.
entries.interpretation: Engineered replacement organs for humans that perform better than their natural counterparts. Examples include artificial red blood cells and super-livers (via genetically engineered organs that overexpress key proteins). Respirocytes, for example, are theoretical artificial red blood cells that carry oxygen 200x more efficiently than red blood cells.

entries.label: Biologically extended senses
entries.claim: Biologically extended senses reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2023
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.7, between the 2022 and 2023 lines, nearer 2023 (read as 2023). Bar from 2021.7 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2022, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Augmentation.
entries.interpretation: The idea is based on the principle that the brain evolved to handle one construction of reality, yet now can overlay multiple local and remote experiences simultaneously, creating new cognitive perceptions. Biological senses can be enhanced and produced artificially, which adapt and transform to address different kinds of stimuli for specific purposes.

entries.label: Machine-augmented cognition
entries.claim: Machine-augmented cognition reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2020
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2020.0, on the 2020 line (read as 2020). Bar from 2019.4 to 2022.5: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2022. Sub-area: Augmentation.
entries.interpretation: Refers to the effective use of information technology to augment human cognition using intelligence amplifying system of tools. Information retrieved from the brain would then be used to feedback necessary stimulus to accomplish determined brain functions. for specific organisms and diseases.

entries.label: Bionic implants
entries.claim: Bionic implants reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2017.6, midway between the 2017 and 2018 lines (read as 2018). Bar from 2015.6 to 2018.8: scientifically viable ~2016, financially viable ~2019. Sub-area: Augmentation.
entries.interpretation: Microscopic technological structures that extract biometric information from an organism to analyze its performance and improve specific biological functions with assisted feedback. In terms of personal biometry, bionic implants represent great tools to empower preventive medicine and develop customized solutions for specific organisms and diseases.

entries.label: Medical nanobots
entries.claim: Medical nanobots reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2027
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.8, between the 2026 and 2027 lines, nearer 2027 (read as 2027). Bar from 2024.9 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2025, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: A subfield of robotics that studies how to make robots that emulate living biological organisms/functions mechanically or chemically. The main objective of this technology applied to medicine is to enhance the human body's capabilities or treat malfunctions with robots capable of re-programming and adapt to different conditions, always mimicking organic functions.

entries.label: Anti-aging drugs
entries.claim: Anti-aging drugs reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2024
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2024.3, between the 2024 and 2025 lines, nearer 2024 (read as 2024). Bar from 2023.0 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2023, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: Breakthroughs in tissue rejuvenation with stem cells, molecular repair, and organ replacement (such as with artificial organs) might eventually enable humans to have indefinite lifespans through complete rejuvenation to a youthful condition.

entries.label: Prenatal gene manipulation
entries.claim: Prenatal gene manipulation reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2023
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.7, between the 2022 and 2023 lines, nearer 2023 (read as 2023). Bar from 2020.2 to 2024.4: scientifically viable ~2020, financially viable ~2024. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: The direct manipulation of an embryo/fetus genome using biotechnology.

entries.label: Epigenetic therapy
entries.claim: Epigenetic therapy reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2022
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.2, between the 2022 and 2023 lines, nearer 2022 (read as 2022). Bar from 2019.0 to 2022.2: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2022. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: The phenomena whereby genetically identical cells express their genes differently resulting in different phenotypes in, for example, the formation of cancer originating from cancer stem cells.

entries.label: Organ printing
entries.claim: Organ printing reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2018.4, midway between the 2018 and 2019 lines (read as 2018). Bar from 2013.8 to 2019.3: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2019. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: The use of a combination of cells, engineering, material methods, and suitable biochemical and physio-chemical factors to improve or replace biological functions. The term is closely associated with applications that repair or replace portions of or whole tissues.

entries.label: Personalized medicine
entries.claim: Personalized medicine reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2017
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2017.1, on the 2017 line (read as 2017). Bar from 2013.8 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Treatments.
entries.interpretation: A branch of genomics where individual genomes are genotyped and analyzed using bioinformatics tools. These may eventually lead to personalized medicine, where patients can take genotype specific drugs for medical treatments.

entries.label: Medical Tricorder
entries.claim: Medical Tricorder reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2023
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.9, on the 2023 line (read as 2023). Bar from 2019.8 to 2025.3: scientifically viable ~2020, financially viable ~2025. Sub-area: Diagnostics.
entries.interpretation: A hypothetical handheld portable scanning device to be used by consumers to self-diagnose medical conditions within seconds and take basic vital measurements. A common view is that it will be a general-purpose tool similar in functionality to a Swiss Army Knife to take health measurements such as blood pressure and temperature and blood flow in a noninvasive way.

entries.label: Biohacking
entries.claim: Biohacking reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2022
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2022.0, on the 2022 line (read as 2022). Bar from 2013.8 to 2022.0: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2022. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Diagnostics.
entries.interpretation: A techno-progressive cultural and intellectual movement which advocates for open access to genetic information and defends the potential of truly democratic technological development. Biohacking can also refer to managing one's own biology using a combination of medical, nutritional and electronic techniques.

entries.label: Labs on chips
entries.claim: Labs on chips reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2018.0, on the 2018 line (read as 2018). Bar from 2013.8 to 2018.0: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2018. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Diagnostics.
entries.interpretation: Devices that integrates one or several laboratory functions on a single chip of only millimeters to a few square centimeters in size. LOCs deal with the handling of extremely small fluid volumes down to less than picoliters. They represent safer platforms for chemical, radioactive or biological studies.

entries.label: Biometric sensors
entries.claim: Biometric sensors reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2015
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2014.9, on the 2015 line (read as 2015). Bar from 2013.7 to 2014.9: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2015. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Diagnostics.
entries.interpretation: The use of biometrics to telecommunications and telecommunications for remote biometric sensing. Potential applications include monitoring blood levels, infections and efficacy of vaccines.

entries.label: Infrastructural health sensors
entries.claim: Infrastructural health sensors reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2025
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2025.3, between the 2025 and 2026 lines, nearer 2025 (read as 2025). Bar from 2021.1 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2021, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Sensors.
entries.interpretation: Can be used for monitoring vibrations and material conditions in buildings, bridges, factories, farms and other infrastructure. Coupled with an intelligent network, such sensors could feed crucial information back to maintenance crews or robots.

entries.label: Livestock biometrics
entries.claim: Livestock biometrics reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2020
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2019.9, on the 2020 line (read as 2020). Bar from 2017.0 to 2020.3: scientifically viable ~2017, financially viable ~2020. Sub-area: Sensors.
entries.interpretation: Collars with GPS, RFID and biometrics can automatically identify and relay vital information about the livestock in real time.

entries.label: Crop sensors
entries.claim: Crop sensors reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2018
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2018.4, between the 2018 and 2019 lines, nearer 2018 (read as 2018). Bar from 2015.7 to 2019.3: scientifically viable ~2016, financially viable ~2019. Sub-area: Sensors.
entries.interpretation: Instead of prescribing field fertilization before application, high-resolution crop sensors inform application equipment of correct amounts needed. Optical sensors or drones are able to identify crop health across the field (for example, by using infra-red light).

entries.label: Equipment telematics
entries.claim: Equipment telematics reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2016
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2016.3, between the 2016 and 2017 lines, nearer 2016 (read as 2016). Bar from 2013.8 to 2017.4: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2017. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Sensors.
entries.interpretation: Allows mechanical devices such as tractors to warn mechanics that a failure is likely to occur soon. Intra-tractor communication can be used as a rudimentary “farm swarm” platform.

entries.label: Air & soil sensors
entries.claim: Air & soil sensors reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2015
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2015.2, between the 2015 and 2016 lines, nearer 2015 (read as 2015). Bar from 2013.8 to 2015.4: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2015. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Sensors.
entries.interpretation: Fundamental additions to the automated farm, these sensors would enable a real time understanding of current farm, forest or body of water conditions.

entries.label: In vitro meat
entries.claim: In vitro meat reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2024
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2023.8, between the 2023 and 2024 lines, nearer 2024 (read as 2024). Bar from 2017.5 to 2027.0: scientifically viable ~2017, financially viable ~2027. Sub-area: Food.
entries.interpretation: Also known as cultured meat or tubesteak, it is a flesh product that has never been part of a complete, living animal. Several current research projects are growing in vitro meat experimentally, although no meat has yet been produced for public consumption.

entries.label: Genetically designed food
entries.claim: Genetically designed food reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2021
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2020.9, on the 2021 line (read as 2021). Bar from 2016.6 to 2022.0: scientifically viable ~2017, financially viable ~2022. Sub-area: Food.
entries.interpretation: The creation of entirely new strains of food animals and plants in order to better address biological and physiological needs. A departure from genetically modified food, genetically designed food would be engineered from the ground up.

entries.label: Robotic farm swarms
entries.claim: Robotic farm swarms reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2026
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.1, on the 2026 line (read as 2026). Bar from 2023.9 to 2026.9: scientifically viable ~2024, financially viable ~2027. Sub-area: Automation.
entries.interpretation: The hypothetical combination of dozens or hundreds of agricultural robots with thousands of microscopic sensors, which together would monitor, predict, cultivate and extract crops from the land with practically no human intervention. Small-scale implementations are already on the horizon.

entries.label: Precision agriculture
entries.claim: Precision agriculture reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2023
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2023.0, on the 2023 line (read as 2023). Bar from 2019.3 to 2023.4: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2023. Sub-area: Automation.
entries.interpretation: Farming management based on observing (and responding to) intra-field variations. With satellite imagery and advanced sensors, farmers can optimize returns on inputs while preserving resources at ever larger scales. Further understanding of crop variability, geolocated weather data and precise sensors should allow improved automated decision-making and complementary planting techniques.

entries.label: Agricultural robots
entries.claim: Agricultural robots reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2020
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2020.2, between the 2020 and 2021 lines, nearer 2020 (read as 2020). Bar from 2018.6 to 2020.7: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2021. Sub-area: Automation.
entries.interpretation: Also known as agbots, these are used to automate agricultural processes, such as harvesting, fruit picking, ploughing, soil maintenance, weeding, planting, irrigation, etc.

entries.label: Rapid iteration selective breeding
entries.claim: Rapid iteration selective breeding reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2017
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2016.9, on the 2017 line (read as 2017). Bar from 2014.3 to 2017.5: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2017. Sub-area: Automation.
entries.interpretation: The next generation of selective breeding where the end-result is analyzed quantitatively and improvements are suggested algorithmically.

entries.label: Variable rate swath control
entries.claim: Variable rate swath control reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2014
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2014.5, midway between the 2014 and 2015 lines (read as 2014). Bar from 2013.8 to 2016.3: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2016. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Automation.
entries.interpretation: Building on existing geolocation technologies, future swath control could save on seed, minerals, fertilizer and herbicides by reducing overlapping inputs. By pre-computing the shape of the field where the inputs are to be used, and by understanding the relative productivity of different areas of the field, tractors or agbots can procedurally apply inputs at variable rates throughout the field.

entries.label: Vertical farming
entries.claim: Vertical farming reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2027
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2026.6, midway between the 2026 and 2027 lines (read as 2027). Bar from 2022.4 to 2027.3: scientifically viable ~2022, financially viable ~2027. The bar reaches the outer edge of the grid (~2027), so financial viability may be at or after the chart end. Sub-area: Engineering.
entries.interpretation: A natural extension of urban agriculture, vertical farms would cultivate plant or animal life within dedicated or mixed-use skyscrapers in urban settings. Using techniques similar to glass houses, vertical farms could augment natural light using energy-efficient lighting.

entries.label: Synthetic biology
entries.claim: Synthetic biology reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2024
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2023.7, between the 2023 and 2024 lines, nearer 2024 (read as 2024). Bar from 2013.8 to 2024.4: scientifically viable ~2014, financially viable ~2024. The bar reaches the inner edge of the grid (~2014), so scientific viability may be at or before the chart start. Sub-area: Engineering.
entries.interpretation: Synthetic biology is about programming biology using standardized parts as one programs computers using standardized libraries today. Includes the broad redefinition and expansion of biotechnology, with the ultimate goals of being able to design, build and remediate engineered biological systems that process information, manipulate chemicals, fabricate materials and structures, produce energy,...

entries.label: Closed ecological systems
entries.claim: Closed ecological systems reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2020
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2019.7, between the 2019 and 2020 lines, nearer 2020 (read as 2020). Bar from 2015.7 to 2022.0: scientifically viable ~2016, financially viable ~2022. Sub-area: Engineering.
entries.interpretation: Ecosystems that do not rely on matter exchange outside the system. Such closed ecosystems would theoretically transform waste products into oxygen, food and water in order to support life-forms inhabiting the system. Such systems already exist in small scales, but existing technological limitations prevent them from scaling.

entries.label: Smart materials
entries.claim: Smart materials reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2026
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2025.6, midway between the 2025 and 2026 lines (read as 2026). Bar from 2021.2 to 2026.8: scientifically viable ~2021, financially viable ~2027. Sub-area: Next-generation.
entries.interpretation: Designed materials that have one or more properties that can be significantly changed in a controlled fashion by external stimuli, such as stress, temperature, moisture, pH, electric or magnetic fields.

entries.label: Thermo-bimetals
entries.claim: Thermo-bimetals reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2021
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2020.9, on the 2021 line (read as 2021). Bar from 2018.9 to 2021.9: scientifically viable ~2019, financially viable ~2022. Sub-area: Next-generation.
entries.interpretation: Thermally activated bimetals would allow for panes of glass capable of becoming shades when exposed to the sun, self-regulating energy consumption throughout the day.

entries.label: Aerogel
entries.claim: Aerogel reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2019
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2019.2, between the 2019 and 2020 lines, nearer 2019 (read as 2019). Bar from 2015.4 to 2020.7: scientifically viable ~2015, financially viable ~2021. Sub-area: Next-generation.
entries.interpretation: A synthetic porous ultralight material derived from a gel, in which the liquid component of the gel has been replaced with a gas. The result is a solid with extremely low density and thermal conductivity which feels like polystyrene (styrofoam) to the touch.

entries.label: Auxetic materials
entries.claim: Auxetic materials reaches R&D prototyping or venture investment around 2017
entries.note: Numbered dot (mainstream point) at 2017.2, between the 2017 and 2018 lines, nearer 2017 (read as 2017). Bar from 2015.9 to 2017.6: scientifically viable ~2016, financially viable ~2018. Sub-area: Next-generation.

Auxetics may be useful in applications such as body armor, packing material, knee and elbow pads, robust shock absorbing material, and sponge mops.

notes: READ BEFORE GRADING: on this poster 'mainstream point' does NOT mean mass adoption. The legend defines it as the point a technology becomes available for prototyping in R&D labs or attracts VC and startup investment, and it sits BEFORE 'financially viable' (products generally available on Kickstarter). The claims use the requested wording '<Name> becomes mainstream around <year>', but the poster's own claim is an early-stage one (R&D prototyping / VC investment). The D10 consumer-mainstream tests would grade it far too strictly. Full methodology box, verbatim: "This piece of research was conducted jointly between Envisioning and Policy Horizons Canada. To conduct the research we scanned the horizon of emerging technologies, deduced probable future developments, speculated about implications and collectively opined about likely timeframes. Each technology timeline indicates soft boundaries for how it might develop in the coming decades. Timelines should be interpreted relatively, not literally. Each technology we create is dependent on every other technology that came before it. Please use the map as a source of inspiration and discovery rather than prophecy." Intro: the map covers 'six key areas' over 'the next 15 years'; the poster says it was commissioned by Policy Horizon Canada and published in MetaScan 3: Emerging Technologies, April 2014. The grid spans only about 2014-2027, so bars reaching either edge are cut by the chart; their end milestone is the edge year and is flagged in the note. Milestones extension: each entry adds 'milestones' {scientifically_viable, mainstream, financially_viable}, rounded years read the same way. The sub-area (inner ring label) is named in each note. Labels and descriptions are transcribed from the side columns, keeping the poster's spelling; interpretation is the description trimmed to 400 characters. The envisioning.com work page is client-rendered, so its text could not be confirmed in an archived copy; the 2014 envisioning.io/horizons snapshot carries the poster's intro and methodology text.
